messages:
maria: quick heads-up, us-west3c GPU pool (az3c) showing elevated NIC errors and ~20% pod evictions since 08:12 UTC. Seen across both c5g/gpu-rt node types. :warning:
kevin: noted. Are we seeing infra-level network flaps or just host-level? any cloud provider health events?
chris: cloud status is OK for region but there are RETRY logs on the top-of-rack switches. SRE saw interface resets on a subset of racks.
maria: confirmed. We're starting a thin drain on impacted racks to avoid noisy neighbor disruption. Plan: cordon -> drain gracefully with cache warm TTL preserved -> reroute traffic.
olivia: tagging dedicated customers with priority >80 to keep them on existing nodes where possible. Lower-priority jobs will be evicted first.
ops-lead: oncall @kevin, @chris, please coordinate sequencing. Suggest draining one rack at a time and warming caches in target AZs before full traffic shift.
tom: agree. Thinking sequence:
1) cordon affected nodes
2) start pod evictions with --grace-period=300
3) spin up replacements in us-west3a/3b and pre-warm KV/cache
4) monitor tail latencies and token cost
kevin: commands I'm running now:
```
# cordon
kubectl cordon gpu-node-az3c-02
# drain with tolerations
kubectl drain gpu-node-az3c-02 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300
```
chris: pre-warming cache on target pool with synthetic workload (small prefix loads). Using the replay harness to replay last 24h hot prefixes.
olivia: cost tradeoff: spinning up new reserved instances in other AZs vs evicting spot-backed capacity. If we scale on reserved it's ~3x cost but keeps SLA for dedicated customers.
maria: short-term choose reserved for critical tenants. Lower tiers use spot and accept throttling.
kevin: noticed a small regression in autoscaler thresholds; scaling delay ~45s. Bumping target utilization to 60% for the transient window.
sre-bot: ALERT: node gpu-node-az3c-05 reported NIC reset x3 in 10m. Marking node as flaky.
tom: if node flapping persists, escalate to cloud provider and start host-replacement. For now draining racks is safer than broad AZ failover.
chris: traffic routing change plan: weighted traffic shift 10% -> 30% -> 60% over 7 minutes with health checks. If error rate >3% rollback one step.
olivia: coordinating customer comms. Sending note to impacted customer list with mitigation ETA ~20-30m. :email: 
ops-lead: let’s keep this thread for sequencing. After we finish first rack drain, post metrics: pod evictions, tail p95 latency, token/sec, model error rate.
maria: first rack cordoned at 08:18 UTC; starting drain now.
kevin: drain finished for rack-7 at 08:24 UTC. No dedicated tenant impact. Warmed caches on us-west3a pool.
chris: rolling weighted shift started 08:27 UTC -> 10% traffic to other AZs.
maria: monitoring p95: +40ms for a short blip, then stabilized. No model error regressions.
olivia: sent customer note at 08:30 UTC. One customer acknowledged and asked for logs; cc'ing support.
tom: recommended postmortem items: add rack-level NIC health alert, reduce autoscaler cool-down during evacuations, and a runbook section for thin-drain sequencing.
kevin: will open infra ticket for reserved burst capacity runbook and update autoscaler config.
ops-lead: update: progress looks good. We'll keep thin-drain strategy; prepare to revert to full AZ evacuation if flapping spreads. Recording this as an incident for follow-up.
maria: thanks team. leaving monitoring on for next 2 hours. ping here if any regressions. :thumbsup:
